questions.question: A person supervising tank loading:

options.text: Does not need to know the materials being loaded.
Must stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A qualified person must watch tank loading with hazardous materials. This person must be alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: Many poisonous products are also:
questions.explanation: Many poisonous products are also flammable. Take proper precautions if your cargo may be flammable.

questions.question: An improperly placarded vehicle can only be moved:

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: A vehicle must be properly placarded before driving. An improperly placarded vehicle can only be moved if it is necessary to protect life or property in an emergency.

questions.question: Do not smoke within ____ of a vehicle placarded for Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded cargo tank carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: How many hazardous materials classes are there?
questions.explanation: There are nine hazardous materials classes. Each class reflects the dangers of that type of material.

questions.question: An improperly placarded vehicle:

options.text: Can only be moved in an emergency.
Can be driven if it does not contain radioactive materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle carrying hazardous materials must be properly placarded to be driven. An improperly placarded vehicle can only be moved if necessary to protect life or property in an emergency.

questions.question: Hazardous materials should be loaded and unloaded:
questions.explanation: Many hazardous materials become more dangerous when heated. Load and unload hazardous materials away from heat sources.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park the vehicle:

options.text: For only short periods of time.

questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building, except briefly for necessary vehicle operations. Never park within five feet of the road. Park only briefly when necessary.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous materials should be:

options.text: Circled by a pen or marker.
Written the same way as the non-hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: When a shipping paper includes both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, highlight the hazardous items in a contrasting color to identify them.

questions.question: Class 7 hazardous material is:
questions.explanation: Radioactive materials are Class 7 hazardous materials.

questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: Where items go on the trailer.
How to load and unload the material.

questions.explanation: There are nine hazard classes. A material's hazard class shows what risks it has.

questions.question: Who must give emergency response information?
questions.explanation: Shippers of hazardous materials must give emergency response information to drivers.

questions.question: Emergency response information from the shipper must include:

options.text: Any risks of fire or explosion.
How many people should respond in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any risks of fire or explosion.
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include descriptions and names of materials being transported, health hazards, fire or explosion risks, precautions in case of accident, how to handle fires, how to handle spills or leaks without fire, and first aid steps.

questions.question: For a HazMat endorsement, which agency must check your background?
questions.explanation: To get or renew a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass a background check from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: When transporting chlorine, what must you keep in the vehicle?

options.text: A phone with emergency numbers saved

questions.explanation: Drivers transporting chlorine in cargo tanks must keep an approved gas mask and an emergency kit in their vehicle.

questions.question: The correct way to check tire pressure is:

options.text: Push on the tire with your hand.

questions.explanation: Check your tires at the start of every trip and after every stop. Use a tire pressure gauge to check if tires are properly filled.

questions.question: On shipping papers, how do you show which items are hazardous?

options.text: List hazardous materials at the bottom.
List hazardous materials at the top.
Highlight hazardous materials in the same color as non-hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: List hazardous materials at the top.
questions.explanation: If shipping papers list both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, show hazardous materials in one of three ways: list them first, highlight them in a different color, or mark them with an "X" in a column labeled "HM."

questions.question: When must a driver take the HazMat knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You must pass the HazMat knowledge test and a federal background check before every CDL renewal.

questions.question: Who decides what hazard class a material belongs to?
questions.explanation: The shipper decides the hazard class, identification number, proper shipping name, and packing group. The shipper also chooses the correct packaging, labels, markings, and placards.

questions.question: How are hazardous materials warnings shown?

options.text: By wrapping the package in orange
By keeping the item away from other cargo and covering it with a sign

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs called placards are placed on vehicles and bulk packages to warn drivers and others about hazardous materials.

questions.question: Where should placards be placed on a truck?

options.text: On the left and right sides

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: What must hazardous materials shipping papers include?

options.text: The intended use of the materials
The country of origin of the materials

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials shipping papers must include an emergency response telephone number so drivers know who to contact in case of an accident.

questions.question: What should a driver check before transporting hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages
The shipping paper is written in code
All packages are labeled as poison
The shipping paper is not in the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages
questions.explanation: Compare the shipping paper to the package markings and labels. Make sure they match.

questions.question: How should hazardous materials be loaded?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials should be loaded away from heat sources. Heat can make these materials more dangerous.

questions.question: What should a driver do if given a leaking package of hazardous materials?

options.text: Leave it on the side of the road
Get someone else to drive it

questions.explanation: Drivers must refuse to transport any leaking packages of hazardous materials.

questions.question: Can Class 3 flammable liquids be moved from one tank to another on a public road?

options.text: Yes, as long as no other people are nearby
No, unless it is an emergency
Yes, but it must be kept secret

questions.correctAnswerText: No, unless it is an emergency
questions.explanation: Flammable liquids should not be transferred between vehicles on a public road unless there is an emergency. Always warn others about the hazardous materials.

questions.question: How far away from a placarded vehicle should a person not smoke?
questions.explanation: No one should smoke within 25 feet of a vehicle carrying Class 3 flammable liquids or Division 2.1 gases. The same rule applies to vehicles carrying explosives, flammable solids, or spontaneously combustible materials.

questions.question: What should a carrier do if hazardous materials are not properly prepared?

options.text: Accept it but note the problem

questions.explanation: Carriers must refuse to transport hazardous materials that are not properly prepared.

questions.question: What does a hazardous materials shipping paper describe?

options.text: How the materials will be transported
Who should accept the materials being transported

questions.explanation: Shipping papers describe the hazardous materials being transported. This includes shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests.

questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers be placed?

options.text: At the bottom of a stack of shipping papers
On top of a stack of shipping papers
In a location separate from non-hazardous materials

questions.correctAnswerText: On top of a stack of shipping papers
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials shipping papers should be placed on top of other shipping papers so drivers can quickly identify them.
